haiku-low.q1: Only a SHA-256 hash (token_hash) is persisted in Postgres. Plaintext exists only in server memory during the create request and the create response shown in the browser dialog, never in Postgres, logs or analytics.
haiku-low.q2: They cannot. Closing the dialog discards the plaintext from the page, and nobody can show it again. The user must revoke that token and create a new one.
haiku-low.q3: The create request gets 409 with the message "Limit reached, revoke a token first." Nothing is inserted.
haiku-low.q4: On its next use. The next API request's lookup finds no row because revoked_at is set, so the server returns 401.
haiku-low.q5: All three receive the same 401, with the same status, headers and generic body. The responses do not differ. Only an internal reason code is logged, never the token.
haiku-low.q6: The server parses the Bearer header, SHA-256 hashes the token, and queries api_tokens by token_hash. The row is usable only if revoked_at is null and expires_at is later than the database now().
haiku-low.q7: A request whose lookup returns stale=true (last_used_at null or over 1 hour old) triggers an UPDATE after the response. The UPDATE repeats the stale condition in its WHERE clause, so concurrent requests cause one effective write.
haiku-low.q8: The API request still succeeds. The server logs the failure without the token and ignores it, so last-used stays stale until the next stale request.
haiku-low.q9: Revoke sets revoked_at = now() in one UPDATE and keeps the row. The list query filters on revoked_at IS NULL, so revoked tokens disappear from the list.
haiku-low.q10: The server returns 404, the same as for an unknown id. Nothing changes, and the response gives no hint whether the id exists for another user.
haiku-low.q11: The row stays committed and counts toward the limit of 10, but the plaintext is lost. The user sees it as Never used in the list, revokes it, and creates a new token. Reusing the name gets 409.

sonnet.q1: It stores the SHA-256 hash (token_hash) plus metadata in Postgres table api_tokens. Plaintext exists only in server memory during the create request and in the create response, shown in the browser dialog. It is never written to Postgres, logs or analytics.
sonnet.q2: They can't. Nobody can show it again, including support and engineering. The server no longer has it. They must revoke it and create a new one.
sonnet.q3: The create returns 409 "Limit reached, revoke a token first". The transaction is rolled back and nothing is inserted.
sonnet.q4: On the very next request. Revoke sets revoked_at = now(), and the auth lookup requires revoked_at IS NULL on every call, with no cache. The next read sees the committed change, so the client gets 401.
sonnet.q5: A generic 401. The responses do not differ: same status, headers and body for unknown, revoked and expired (and also missing or malformed) tokens. An internal reason code may be logged, never the token.
sonnet.q6: The server checks the header is pat_ plus 32 characters, computes the SHA-256 hash, and looks up api_tokens by token_hash. The record is usable only if revoked_at IS NULL and expires_at > now() (database clock). If no row matches, it returns 401.
sonnet.q7: A write is triggered only when the lookup's stale flag is true: last_used_at IS NULL or older than 1 hour. The UPDATE repeats that same condition in its WHERE clause, so concurrent requests produce only one effective write. That limits it to about one write per token per hour.
sonnet.q8: Nothing happens to the request. The update runs after the response is sent. The failure is logged (without the token) and ignored, and the request still succeeds. Last-used stays stale until the next stale request.
sonnet.q9: Revoke sets revoked_at = now() on the row with a single UPDATE. The list query filters revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(), so the revoked token disappears from the list. The row stays in the table.
sonnet.q10: The server returns 404 with no state change. The UPDATE has WHERE id AND user_id = session user AND revoked_at IS NULL, so 0 rows are affected. This is the same 404 as for an unknown id.
sonnet.q11: The row is committed and counts toward the limit of 10, but the plaintext is gone and can't be resent. The user finds it in the list with "Never" as last used, revokes it, and creates a new one. Retrying with the same name returns 409.
